skill.name: deep-research
skill.description: Split complex research questions into focused searches and run them in parallel when subagents are available. Combine verified findings into a cited report that identifies unresolved questions.
skill.summary: Turn research from multiple angles into one cited report.

content.user_title: Research Complex Topics and Verify Sources
content.value_statement: Complex research questions often require comparing evidence across several sources. This skill splits the work into focused searches and combines verified findings into a cited report.
actual_capabilities: Breaks broad questions into three to five distinct tracks, with smaller groups on slower models.
Runs tracks in parallel when subagents are available and searches directly when they are not.
Checks key claims against primary sources and collects supporting quotes or source figures.
Limits each worker's search effort and uses a targeted follow-up for important gaps.
Writes a report with inline links, a two-sentence summary, and a section for unresolved evidence when needed.
limitations: Parallel work requires subagent support, and live page reads depend on the browser tools available in the session.
The workflow cannot guarantee access to sources or complete coverage within its search budget.
Simple factual questions do not benefit from the full research workflow.
The workflow does not define what restricted source material may be included in a report.

use_cases.title: Survey Transit Policies
use_cases.description: Compare how several cities set youth fares using public agency policies and list any differences in eligibility.

use_cases.title: Verify Claims for an Article
use_cases.description: Trace published statistics to their original studies and flag figures that use different populations or time periods.

use_cases.title: Compare Procurement Options
use_cases.description: Review public documentation for several suppliers and separate documented support terms from claims without a source.

prompt_templates.title: Survey a Topic
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Get a short overview from public sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Survey how public libraries lend digital books. Use public library sources and summarize the main lending models with links.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Published Policies
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Compare options using the same criteria.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare youth fares in Seattle, Portland, and San Francisco as of October 2026. Use official transit sources and explain age limits, proof requirements, and route exclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Conflicting Figures
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Trace discrepancies to their original sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare recent estimates of food waste from public agencies. Trace each figure to its original report and explain which differences come from definitions or measurement years.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Decision Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Research independent tracks and resolve evidence gaps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare three library lending platforms across accessibility, licensing, and renewal rules. Use separate research tracks and public primary sources. Verify any figures that affect the recommendation and list unresolved gaps.

output_examples.input: Compare youth fare eligibility across three cities.
output_examples.output: Illustrative summary: Agencies use different age limits and proof requirements. The comparison lists each policy separately and marks any rule the agency has not published.

output_examples.input: Explain why two public reports give different food waste estimates.
output_examples.output: Illustrative finding: One report counts household waste only, while the other includes retail waste. Unresolved: The sources do not provide a shared breakdown for a direct comparison.

best_practices: Specify the decision, geographic scope, and date range before starting a broad investigation.
Ask for primary sources and distinguish verified findings from unresolved claims.
Use public sources by default and confirm permissions before accessing or quoting restricted material.
anti_patterns: Using parallel research for a single fact that one reliable source can answer.
Treating search snippets as evidence without checking the original source.
Quoting authenticated pages in a shared report without permission.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for broad surveys, comparisons, or questions that need evidence from several independent sources.

faq.question: What happens when subagents are unavailable?
faq.answer: The assistant handles the search tracks directly instead of assigning them to parallel workers.

faq.question: How does it handle conflicting evidence?
faq.answer: The report can use a targeted follow-up to check important gaps and lists conflicts that remain unresolved.

faq.question: Can it use pages that require sign-in?
faq.answer: The workflow can request browser access when tools and permissions allow it. Confirm that access and any use of the material are authorized.

faq.question: Where does the report appear?
faq.answer: It uses the session artifact directory when available. Headless runs return the report directly.

faq.question: Does the report guarantee complete coverage?
faq.answer: No. Search budgets limit coverage, and the report identifies important gaps that remain.
